title: Sugar and Spite
intro: The night before the Wrenhaven Bake-Off, Maud Penhallow's showstopper, four tiers of lemon and lavender, was found face-down on her bakery floor.
Maud locked up at 20:30 and came back for her reading glasses at 21:15. The back door's lock is stiff, so whoever did it was inside for at least five minutes.
Three people had a reason to hate that cake. Each of them has a story.

people.name: Agnes Trelawney
people.blurb: Rival baker. Runner-up three years running. Says she doesn't mind.

people.name: Bram Okafor
people.blurb: Maud's apprentice. Wants his name on the loaves, not just flour on his apron.

people.name: Clem Hollis
people.blurb: Caterer, chess fiend, Maud's ex-husband. Still has a key.

incident.title: The Showstopper
incident.text: Maud's Bake-Off cake was tipped off its stand inside Penhallow's Bakery. Locked at 20:30, found at 21:15. The vandal needed 5 minutes inside.

cards.title: Agnes Trelawney
cards.text: “I went to the quarter-past-eight picture at the Odeon and didn't come out till half nine. Sat through every minute of it.”
cards.reply: “…Oh, all right. I was in the Lantern. Two sherries. If the judges hear I was tippling the night before the Bake-Off, I'll never live it down.”

cards.title: Bar tab
cards.text:
Mrs A. TRELAWNEY
2 × sweet sherry
Settled at the bar.

cards.title: Sid Barrow
cards.text: “Agnes came in about twenty to nine and sat at the end of the bar till gone half nine. Never left her stool.”
cards.firm: “She never shifted. I'd have noticed. She was blocking the dartboard.”

cards.title: Bram Okafor
cards.text: “I was playing chess with Clem at the Harbour Café from half eight till twenty past nine. He beat me twice. Ask him.”
cards.reply: “Fine. I left the café. I went for a walk. I needed matches… for my stove. That's not a crime.”

cards.title: Clem Hollis
cards.text: “Bram and I were at the café over the chessboard, half eight till twenty past nine. Neither of us left the table.”
cards.reply: “All right. I left at a quarter to nine for the bus to my sister's. Bram asked me to say we were together all evening. He said he had an ‘errand’. I didn't ask.”

cards.title: Bus ticket
cards.text:
Single, adult. Clipped by the conductor at the depot.
Found in C. Hollis's coat pocket.

cards.title: Clem Hollis (again)
cards.text: “We played from half eight till a quarter to nine. Then I went for my bus and Bram went off on his errand.”
cards.firm: “That's the truth this time. Quarter to nine. I nearly missed the bus.”

cards.title: Till receipt
cards.text:
1 × Swan Vestas matches
ON ACCOUNT: B. OKAFOR

triggers.question: Agnes says she was at the pictures, but her bar tab puts her in the Lantern at 20:52. Which is it?
Clem swears he never left the chessboard, so how was his bus ticket clipped at the depot at 21:10?
Bram was buying matches at Fenwick's at 21:12 while ‘playing chess at the café’?

memos.text: Every card belongs somewhere. Drag each one onto the board. It'll find its own line and its own time.
The ribbons show the walk between places. Ink blue: there was time. Red: there wasn't.
Red means impossible. Paper doesn't lie, people do. Click a statement in the red and confront them.
A lie isn't a confession. People lie about sherry, sweethearts and debts. Ask where they really were.
Now drag the incident card across the lines. It'll only fit where someone had the time to do it.

reconstruction: 20:45. Clem leaves for his bus. Bram leaves the café right behind him.
20:59. Bram lets himself into the bakery with the spare key from the flour bin.
21:01. Four tiers of lemon and lavender meet the floor.
21:12. Matches at Fenwick's, on account. He thought that made an alibi.
epilogue: Bram confessed before Maud had finished sweeping up. She'd told him, again, that he wasn't ready to bake under the Penhallow name.
Maud entered a plain Victoria sponge instead and won anyway. Agnes came second and swore it was the sherry.
Connie's note on the file: “Good work, partner. Next time the clocks won't be on your side.”
